evidence: Defining behavior is graded heavily in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: wall_every_route (4.0, lines 54-67), wall_mentions_and_links (4.0), wall_added_live (2.0), deleted_and_expired_messages (4.0), timer_changes (4.0), hold_scope_and_release (2.0), plus threads/edits/search/transcript, matching the brief's 'Two things matter more than anything else' (walls, retention). Durability: persistence criterion (judge.toml lines 266-280) sets up messages, replies, edit+earlier version, hold, deletion, M-12 timer and Sian's wall, requires them as positive controls before restart (step c), then calls restart_app (a real process kill/relaunch on the same DB_PATH via template-identical test.sh lines 127-193 and restart_mcp.py), opens a fresh page, re-signs in and requires every noted item to match; this covers every durable item the brief lists in integration.md ('messages, replies, edits and their versions, timers, holds, walls, unread positions and deletions'), including Dev's exact M-13 unread count, and the Survey/Probate/Insurer search counts detect a seed re-import on restart. Server-backed (not same-origin): constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml lines 76-88) posts as Gwen, reloads, and reads back as Harriet in a separate browser context, so a localStorage/client-only facade fails the gate; app_context.md line 24 gives the feasible newContext recipe. Weak-app probes: an in-memory server passes the gate but fails persistence (JUDGE-S0 lost); an app persisting messages but keeping unread/walls/timers in memory fails on Dev's count, Sian's not-available or the 30-day timer; an app that re-imports seed each start changes the Survey/Probate/Insurer counts. Conforming alternative: invalidating sessions on restart is tolerated (fresh sign-in required); any storage layout passes since only browser-visible state is compared. Runtime: scripted golden run (hashes verified) shows persistence_before PASS and persistence PASS across a real kill (restart-pids old 28 -> new 57). Risk=true because no configured judge run exists on these v3 bytes: the hosted Oracle/model runs that scored persistence 1.0 used the PREVIOUS v2 wording (which lacked the step-c positive-control requirement), so v3 persistence judge feasibility within its 550 s per-criterion cap is unmeasured; the scripted golden also checks Sian/Dev not-available via direct API status 404 rather than through the browser.
